annotations.title: Settle a security deposit after move-out

description:
Settles a US residential security deposit after move-out under the state's statute (50 states and DC) and a covered city's ordinance. Inputs: state, deposit_usd, vacated_on; optional city, monthly_rent_usd, move_in_on, deductions (category, amount, item age, whether the tenant caused it), the dates that start a state's clock, and as_of. Returns the return deadline and its status, each deduction allowed or not (with depreciation), interest owed, refund due, penalty exposure, a draft itemized statement and a citation for every rule. Not for: legal advice, tenant demand letters, repair cost estimates, pet deposits, rentals outside the US.
Deterministic and source-cited: the same input gives the same result.

amount_usd.description: Amount you intend to deduct, in dollars (rounded to cents).

category.description: One of: unpaid_rent, unpaid_utilities, cleaning, carpet, flooring, paint, blinds_window_coverings, appliance, fixture_or_hardware, wall_or_door_repair, key_or_lock, late_fees, lease_break_fee, moving_and_storage, reletting_costs (advertising or a broker to re-rent after an early move-out), trash_and_abandoned_items (removing trash or belongings left behind), other_damage, other. Carpet cleaning is cleaning (with cleaning_kind), not carpet.

caused_by_tenant.description: False when the condition is normal wear and tear (never deductible); null when it is disputed or unknown (a tenant checking a landlord's list): the line is then 'depends', with the amount the rule would allow if it is damage.

cleaning_kind.description: cleaning only: beyond_wear (the unit was left dirtier than normal use; cleaning to restore its move-in condition), routine (ordinary cleaning after normal use, which most states treat as normal wear) or unknown. Where the statute does not name cleaning, an unknown kind is 'depends'.

description.description: What was damaged or owed and the repair or charge (e.g. 'bedroom carpet: pet stains, two areas patched'). Printed under the line on the itemized statement you download (HTML or PDF); never stored, logged or hashed, and not in the result.

good_faith_estimate.description: The amount is a good-faith estimate: the repair cannot reasonably be finished within the return period, or the vendor's bills have not arrived (California 1950.5(h)(3)). The receipts then follow within 14 days of the repair or the documents.

has_photos.description: You have photos of this damage.

has_receipt.description: You have a receipt, invoice or estimate for this line.

item_age_years.description: Age of the item in years at move-out (e.g. 4.5).

item_installed_on.description: When the item (carpet, paint, appliance...) was installed or last replaced (YYYY-MM-DD). Give this or item_age_years, not both.

late_payments.description: late_fees only: how many late payments (or months, where the cap is per month) the fee covers. A statutory cap is per late payment; without this, more than one cap is 'depends'.

rent_through.description: unpaid_rent only: the last day the rent charged covers. With new_tenant_moved_in_on it decides how much of the rent overlaps the new tenancy (not recoverable: the landlord cannot collect rent twice for the same days).

useful_life_years.description: Override the useful life used for depreciation (years).

utility_kind.description: unpaid_utilities only: which utility. Some states allow only some (Massachusetts: water); without it such a line is 'depends'.

work_kind.description: repair (restores the item: never depreciated), replace (a new item: prorated by the old one's remaining life where the rule does), or cleaning (e.g. carpet cleaning: judged as a cleaning line).

cleaning_notice.description: You gave the tenant written notice of the cleaning needed and time to do it before charging for cleaning (Montana 70-25-201(3): 24 hours).

itemized_statement.description: You will send (or sent) an itemized statement.

move_in_condition_statement.description: You gave the tenant a written move-in condition statement or checklist (Montana 70-25-206, Washington 59.18.260; listed as a duty in Georgia 44-7-33(a), Kentucky 383.580(2), Michigan 554.608 and Virginia 55.1-1214).

move_out_list.description: You inspected the unit and made the move-out damage list in time (Georgia 44-7-33(b): within 3 business days).

receipts.description: You have receipts or invoices for the repairs and cleaning.

Returned.description:
What the landlord has returned so far: lets the result say whether the refund and the
itemized statement came on time (``timeliness``).

method.description: How the money went back: check, electronic (direct deposit or electronic transfer) or other. Some statutes key on it (Michigan 554.609(3): an electronic balance may follow the notice by 10 days; California 1950.5 as amended by AB 414: electronic return when the deposit or rent was paid electronically).

on.description: Day it was sent or delivered (YYYY-MM-DD); required unless what is nothing. Statutes count the day the landlord mails or delivers it; a postmark is the best evidence.

what.description: nothing: nothing returned yet; full_refund: the whole deposit; partial_refund: part of it, with no itemized statement; itemized_statement: an itemized statement of deductions (with any refund the same day).

as_of.description: Today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the deadline status. Defaults to today (UTC); send it for repeatable results.

audit.description: Also return the run record and input/result hashes (an audit trail). Default false.

building_units.description: Units in the building. Some interest rules depend on it (NY 6+, IL 25+).

city.description: City, for a city overlay where covered (e.g. 'Chicago'). Optional.

claim_notice_sent_on.description: Day you sent the written notice of intent to impose a claim on the deposit (YYYY-MM-DD). Florida (due within 30 days of termination) and the District of Columbia (within 45 days): the balance is due 30 days after it; a late notice does not count.

client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

contractor_needed.description: Damage exceeds the deposit and needs a third-party contractor, and you said so in writing in time (Virginia, West Virginia: 15 more days).

county.description: Tennessee only: the county the unit is in (the landlord-tenant act applies only in counties over 75,000 by the 2010 census, 66-28-102(a)). Taken from the city when it lies in one county.

deductions.description: What you intend to deduct (or, for a tenant, what the landlord listed). An explicit empty list means nothing is deducted (it decides the shorter no-deduction periods, e.g. Montana 10 days, Alaska 14); leave it out when that is not known yet.

demand_received_on.description: Day you received the tenant's demand for the deposit (YYYY-MM-DD; written in Oklahoma, by first-class mail in Maryland 8-203(h)). Arizona, Kansas, Oklahoma, South Carolina and Mississippi start the clock on it.

deposit_collected_on.description: Day the deposit was collected (YYYY-MM-DD); defaults to move_in_on. California (AB 12, from 2024-07-01) and Colorado caps depend on it.

deposit_in_separate_account.description: Tennessee only (66-28-301(a)): the deposit was kept in a separate account used only for deposits. No account and no damage listing means none of it can be kept (66-28-301(c)).

documentation.description: What documentation you have; leave a field out when unknown.

expect_ruleset.description: Optional. The ruleset version you built against, as results carry it in provenance.ruleset_version (e.g. 'sd-2026.11.14'), or its sha256: hash. If the rules have changed since, the call fails (nothing computed, nothing charged) and says what is in force now, so you upgrade on your own schedule. Leave it out to answer under the current rules.

forwarding_address_received_on.description: Day you received the tenant's written forwarding address (YYYY-MM-DD). Several states start or hold the clock on it (Texas, Connecticut, Iowa, Minnesota).

furnished.description: The unit is rented furnished (California before AB 12: 3 months; Kansas: 1.5 months; Delaware: no cap).

interest_paid_through.description: Interest already paid or credited to the tenant up to this day (annual-payment rules: San Francisco, Los Angeles, Berkeley, Connecticut, Massachusetts, ...): interest is counted from it.

interest_rate_percent.description: Annual rate the deposit account paid, where the law sets interest at the bank's rate (New Jersey, North Dakota, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania, Portland), or caps it (Massachusetts: 5% or the bank's lesser rate). Without it bank-rate interest is unknown. Illinois 765 ILCS 715 uses IDFPR's published rate instead.

landlord_filed_action_on.description: Michigan only (YYYY-MM-DD): day the landlord sued for the damages claimed (554.613: sue or return the balance within 45 days). Not given: no suit assumed.

landlord_units_owned.description: Rental units the landlord owns in all (Arkansas 5 or fewer, Georgia 10 or fewer, with third_party_managed, may be exempt).

lease_end_on.description: Day the lease was scheduled to end (YYYY-MM-DD), when it differs from when the tenancy actually ended (a broken lease). Lost rent and lease-break charges run to it; deadlines do not (they follow tenancy_ended_on, else the move-out, with the scheduled end as a later alternative).

lease_return_days.description: Return period the lease sets, in days, where the statute lets a lease set one (Colorado up to 60, Idaho up to 30, Maine shorter).

lease_signed_or_renewed_on.description: Day the current lease was signed or last renewed (YYYY-MM-DD). Georgia (2024-07-01) and Maryland (2024-10-01) caps apply to leases from then; defaults to move_in_on, with a warning that a later renewal may bring the new cap.

lease_term_months.description: Term of the lease in months (0 for month-to-month). Delaware's cap applies to leases of a year or more, New Mexico's to shorter ones.

monthly_rent_usd.description: Monthly rent, for the deposit cap check.

move_in_on.description: Tenancy start (YYYY-MM-DD). Used for interest and, when an item's age is unknown, for depreciation.

new_tenant_moved_in_on.description: Day a new tenant moved in, if the unit was re-rented (YYYY-MM-DD). West Virginia and Wisconsin can end the period earlier; rent claimed for days from it on is not recoverable (re-rent mitigation).

new_tenant_rent_usd.description: Monthly rent the new tenant pays (with new_tenant_moved_in_on): the rent received for overlapping days is credited against rent claimed for them.

nonstandard_provision_signed.description: Wisconsin: the tenant signed a separate NONSTANDARD RENTAL PROVISIONS document covering the charge (ATCP 134.06(3)(b)); false makes such charges 'no'.

owner_is_natural_person.description: Georgia only (44-7-36): the units are owned by a natural person (false: an LLC, corporation, partnership or trust owns them). The small-landlord exemption reaches only a natural person; not given, the statute is shown with the exemption as the alternative.

owner_occupied.description: The landlord lives in the building (ME, NH, NJ and Chicago exempt small owner-occupied buildings; with building_units).

pet_deposit_usd.description: The part of deposit_usd that is a pet deposit (outside the cap in Missouri, Alabama, North Dakota and Saint Paul; allowed on top of it up to one month in Hawaii and Alaska, half a month in Kansas, a quarter in Nebraska).

prepaid_rent_usd.description: Rent paid in advance beyond the first month, held besides deposit_usd. Counts toward the cap in AK, AZ, CA, CT, MD, MI and NY; earns interest in CT, MA (last month's rent), MD and Chicago; in Minneapolis it lowers the deposit cap to half a month. In UT its balance is returned with the deposit and counted in the refund (57-17-3(2)(b)): send only the unused part (rent already applied to a rental period is not a balance). Elsewhere the refund covers the deposit only and a warning says unused prepaid rent is owed back too.

rent_ordinance_covered.description: The unit is covered by the city's rent ordinance (Los Angeles RSO, Berkeley Rent Ordinance). Their deposit interest is owed only then; unknown: the amount is shown beside the refund, not in it.

renter_notice_served_on.description: Utah only (YYYY-MM-DD): day the renter served the 57-17-3(3) notice after the deadline passed. The owner then has five business days to comply (57-17-3(5)); without the notice there is no relief under 57-17-5.

returned.description: What the landlord has returned so far and when. With it, timeliness says whether the refund and the itemized statement were on time and how many days late.

serve_pinned.description: Optional, with expect_ruleset. True asks us to answer under the ruleset version you named even when the rules have changed since, from that version's signed bundle; the result says so in served_from_bundle. We refuse a version older than 12 months, one a later correction or law change replaced for your state, or one we have no bundle for. Default false: the call fails whenever the rules have changed.

small_landlord.description: California AB 12 small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning at most two properties with at most four units; not for a service member): a two-month cap.

state.description: US state, 2-letter code (e.g. 'CA'); a state name also works.

statement_sent_on.description: Day you sent (or delivered) the itemized statement (YYYY-MM-DD). With it the statement is judged on time or late; documentation.itemized_statement alone cannot tell.

tenancy_ended_on.description: When the tenancy actually ended (YYYY-MM-DD): the lease's end, or an earlier termination or accepted surrender. Deadlines that run from the end of the tenancy use it. For a tenant who left before the lease was due to end, send the scheduled end as lease_end_on (older callers sent it here, which still works: the deadline is then counted from it, with the move-out date as an earlier alternative where the facts point to one).

tenancy_type.description: written_lease or at_will (Maine 6033(2): a written agreement's period, at most 30 days, or 21 days for a tenancy at will; Massachusetts 15B(4): at will, 30 days after the move-out, a written lease, 30 days after its end). Left out with a move-out before tenancy_ended_on: the earlier (at-will) date leads and the other is listed.

tenant_abandoned.description: The tenant abandoned the unit or was evicted (Maryland 8-203(h): the clock runs from the tenant's written demand; Washington 59.18.280: from when the landlord learns of it; Louisiana 9:3251(C): the one-month rule does not apply). Left out: inferred from tenant_gave_proper_notice: false; with a move-out before tenancy_ended_on the earlier abandonment clock leads and the other date is listed.

tenant_age_60_plus.description: A person 60 or older occupies the unit (New Hampshire 540-A:5, I: the owner-occupied exemption does not reach the unit). tenant_age_62_plus true implies it.

tenant_age_62_plus.description: The tenant is 62 or older (Connecticut: a one-month cap).

tenant_gave_forwarding_address.description: False when the tenant never gave a forwarding address in writing (not just 'not yet known'). Illinois, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Delaware, South Carolina and New Hampshire then relieve the landlord of the penalty. Implied true by forwarding_address_received_on.

tenant_gave_proper_notice.description: A termination notice that meets the statute was given (Alaska: 14 days instead of 30 when nothing is deducted for damage).

third_party_managed.description: A third party manages the unit or collects rent for a fee.

vacated_on.description: Day the tenant moved out and returned possession (YYYY-MM-DD).

name: deposit_settlement_settle
title: Settle a security deposit after move-out
